citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121.
creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
description: TOFU (Task of Fictitious Unlearning) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating machine unlearning in large language models. It consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, generated by GPT-4 based on predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, and parents' professions. The dataset is used to finetune LLMs and then evaluate unlearning methods that attempt to make models forget specific subsets (forget sets) of these fictitious author profiles.
name: TOFU
rai:dataBiases: Initial experimentation without seeded attributes showed that GPT-4 exhibited strong biases: most author birth years clustered between 1970 and 1980 (particularly August 1975), most book titles contained words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers', and most authors had similar upbringings with 'magical' writing styles. To mitigate these biases, the final dataset uses an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds author attributes and draws book title keywords from the Goodreads Books dataset.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate synthetic author biographies. Each author profile was seeded with predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards, parents' professions, and book title keywords). GPT-4 was then tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author. Book title keywords were drawn from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle to ensure diversity across genres.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of GPT-4-generated question-answer pairs about 200 fictitious author profiles. Each profile was generated based on seed attributes including birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards, and parents' professions. Book title keywords were sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to entity-level forgetting and does not cover instance-level or behavior-level unlearning. It only considers unlearning of information learned during finetuning, not pretraining. The benchmark provides exact forget and retain sets, which may not reflect real-world scenarios where identifying the forget/retain sets is itself a challenge. In-context unlearning is also out of scope. The benchmark does not address alignment to human values.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An elaborate prompt was used to deterministically seed various author attributes (place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, parents' occupation, book title keywords) to minimize bias leakage from GPT-4's pretraining data. Book title keywords were randomly selected from two books per genre from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle to ensure diversity. An initial dummy set of 50 authors was generated with a generic prompt and found to have biased word distributions; the final dataset used the seeded prompt to address this.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to help address privacy concerns in LLMs, specifically the Right to be Forgotten. By providing a controlled benchmark for unlearning, it aims to support the development of methods that protect private data in deployed LLMs, which is relevant to emerging regulations such as GDPR and CCPA. The paper highlights that existing unlearning methods are largely ineffective, motivating further research into privacy-preserving AI.
rai:dataUseCases: TOFU is intended as a benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning methods in large language models, specifically for the Right to be Forgotten use case. It is designed to help researchers develop and evaluate unlearning algorithms that can make LLMs forget specific information (fictitious author profiles) while preserving general model utility.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate all question-answer pairs for the fictitious author profiles. GPT-4 was also used to generate paraphrased answers and factually incorrect perturbations of answers for use in the Truth Ratio evaluation metric.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset is synthetically generated by GPT-4, not annotated by human annotators; no per-item annotation count is described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators were used; data was generated by GPT-4.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No human annotation was performed; data was synthetically generated by GPT-4.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform was used; data was synthetically generated by GPT-4.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol; data was generated via GPT-4 prompting described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data in the paper; the dataset is fully synthetic and generated to completion.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset is fully synthetic with no missing values to impute.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection manipulation protocol described for the dataset itself (unlearning algorithms are applied to models, not the dataset).
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains only fictitious author profiles with no real personal or sensitive information.
